title: Insight lab: nothing strong this week
why: Saturday run, 31 Oct 2026: a second, independent sample of 219 homepages (no overlap with Monday's 213). Nothing new is strong enough to publish. The replication changes the wording of Monday's WordPress cards.
body:
RESULT: no new content this week.

REPLICATION OF MONDAY'S CARD (WordPress schema gap):
- Holds: WordPress homepages score 5.3 points higher (95% interval 2.0 to 8.6; 108 vs 111 sites). After removing the three schema checks, the gap is 0.7 (interval -2.0 to 3.3). Pooled over both samples (432 homepages): 6.1 points (3.8 to 8.4), of which schema is nearly all. Content schema passes on 74% of WordPress homepages vs 27% of the rest in both samples.
- Does not hold: "WordPress beats modern stacks." Next.js homepages tie WordPress in both samples (84.9 and 83.2). Webflow moved from 77.4 to 82.1. Against identified non-WordPress platforms, the gap is 4.0 (1.7 to 6.4), under our 5-point rule. Most of the gap comes from sites whose platform we could not detect.
- Suggested correction before you post the X thread (insight-2026-W44-1-x-r2): replace the hook "We expected Webflow and custom builds to beat WordPress on AI readiness. They did not." with "WordPress homepages scored higher on AI readiness in two samples of small B2B sites. Almost the whole gap is schema the SEO plugin adds by default." Apply the same framing to the LinkedIn r2 and the blog outline. The Monday morning step stays as written.

DISCARDED THIS WEEK:
1. Cloudflare's managed robots.txt causes most AI-crawler blocking (5 of 8 blocking sites). Do not publish: n=5, 0 such sites on Monday, and the file states a no-training policy the owner may have chosen. Scoring note: each such site loses 16 of 26 access points.
2. Segment gaps (SaaS vs agency vs professional services): all under 1 point this week. Monday's 4.5-point agency gap did not reproduce.
3. Technical and trust pillars move together (r = 0.53): the schema checks sit in both pillars, so this is the WordPress finding again.
4. Crawler access as the biggest single fix: mostly ordinary admin-path Disallow rules scored as limited. The check needs your review first.

METHOD: 244 domains found by web search, not random, so likely more SEO-active than average; 219 scored on 31 Oct 2026, homepage only, one scan each, from a data-center address. 12 of 19 failures were host bot challenges. Readiness only.
